citations.anchor: it('keeps the first pool, and silently keeps the first config with it'
citations.why: A second initDatabase with a different connection string and poolMax leaves getPool() identical to the first pool and its options unchanged, so a second pool/Drizzle client per process would fail here.

citations.anchor: it('closes once the last holder shuts down'
citations.why: Two inits then two shutdowns end the pool, and one shutdown does not — the only way that holds is if the repeat init incremented the holder counter.

citations.anchor: it('names the mistake instead of returning undefined'
citations.why: Asserts both getDatabase() and getPool() throw the exact 'Database not initialized. Call initDatabase() first.' message before any init.

citations.anchor: it('opens the pool with an explicit ceiling and an explicit wait'
citations.why: Reads the live pool's options on a booted app and asserts max is set and connectionTimeoutMillis is both the documented value and strictly greater than zero.

citations.anchor: it('fails a checkout it cannot serve instead of waiting forever'
citations.why: Holds all DEFAULT_POOL_MAX clients and asserts the next query rejects with a timeout near the configured bound — the 'error on one request, not an unbounded wait' half.

citations.anchor: it('leaves the pool alone while a second application still holds it'
citations.why: Two inits then one shutdown hook: asserts pool.ended is false and getPool() still returns the same pool, so a neighbour in the process keeps its database.

citations.anchor: it('closes once the last holder shuts down'
citations.why: The complementary half — after the second shutdown the pool is ended and the memo cleared, so the last holder out does close the door.

citations.anchor: it('clears the memo so a later init really opens a new pool'
citations.why: After closeDatabase a fresh initDatabase yields a pool that is not the first object and carries the new poolMax, which is only possible if the memo was cleared before end().

citations.anchor: it('never throws out of the hook'
citations.why: Makes Pool.end reject and asserts onApplicationShutdown still resolves while Logger.error was called with the failure — exception swallowed, only logged.

citations.anchor: it('runs the callback in one transaction, and a nested run joins it'
citations.why: Compares txid_current() read inside the outer and the nested run and asserts they are equal, and that the nested executor is the same object — a second BEGIN would give a different txid.

citations.anchor: it('reports whether a unit of work is active, and hands out the base connection outside one'
citations.why: Outside run, isActive() is false and uow.current().execute(...) runs a real query against the pool without throwing.

citations.anchor: it('refuses an append outside a unit of work instead of committing it alone'
citations.why: Asserts append outside run rejects with 'must be called inside UnitOfWork.run' and that no row landed in outbox_events.

citations.anchor: it('rolls the appended events back with the state change that produced them'
citations.why: Throws after append inside run and asserts the outbox holds nothing for that aggregate — the rollback half.

citations.anchor: it('commits the events with the state change that produced them'
citations.why: A committing run leaves exactly the two appended rows visible — the commit half.

citations.anchor: it('is a no-op for an empty event array'
citations.why: append([]) inside a run resolves; without the early return Drizzle's insert().values([]) would throw, so the 'no query, no error' pair is what makes this pass.

citations.anchor: it('rejects the whole unit of work when one append repeats an eventId'
citations.why: Asserts the run rejects with Postgres error 23505 (unique violation on the uuid primary key) and that the aggregate's outbox rows are all gone.

citations.anchor: it('commits the token and its event together, and survives a dead dispatcher'
citations.why: suspendOutboxDispatch makes the post-commit drain throw; the mint still returns 201 and the token is listable, and the event sits undispatched rather than lost.

citations.anchor: it('picks up a row nothing asked it to, once the poll backstop is running'
citations.why: Pins the recovery clause: with the backstop stopped nothing is delivered, and once onApplicationBootstrap restarts it the row is delivered with no drain call.

citations.anchor: it('claims the oldest batch, delivers it, and stamps what it delivered'
citations.why: Exactly the 100 rows the subscriber saw are the ones with dispatched_at set, so a stamp that did not follow delivery would fail.

citations.anchor: it('increments attempts and leaves the row pending when a subscriber throws'
citations.why: The 'only after finishing without throwing' half: a throwing subscriber leaves dispatched_at NULL across two drains.

citations.anchor: it('increments attempts and leaves the row pending when a subscriber throws'
citations.why: Pins the increment-and-stay-undelivered clause (attempts 2 after two drains, dispatched_at NULL); the 'the batch's other rows are delivered normally' clause is not pinned — no suite mixes a failing and a succeeding row inside one claimed batch.

citations.anchor: it('spaces retries out instead of burning the ceiling at commit rate'
citations.why: Pins the next_attempt_at clause: after the first failure the row's next_attempt_at is in the future and back-to-back drains do not re-call the subscriber.

citations.anchor: it('stops claiming a row once it has failed MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS times'
citations.why: Drains MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS + 3 times with retries forced due and asserts the subscriber was called exactly MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS times and attempts stopped climbing — the row left the selection.

citations.anchor: it('does not let a full batch of poison rows starve the events behind them'
citations.why: 100 parked rows at the head of the queue plus two newer healthy ones: the healthy pair is still delivered, which is exactly the head-of-line clause.

citations.anchor: it('never schedules a retry in the past'
citations.why: Asserts nextAttemptAfter(n, now) > now for every n from 1 to MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS.

citations.anchor: it('doubles with each further failure'
citations.why: Pins the curve's shape from the 1-second base: 2s, 4s, 8s, 128s for attempts 2, 3, 4, 8.

citations.anchor: it('plateaus at five minutes rather than running away'
citations.why: Asserts the delay caps at 300000ms at the ceiling and stays there for an absurd attempt count.

citations.anchor: it('collapses concurrent drains instead of running one per caller'
citations.why: Five simultaneous drain() calls over a 500-row backlog deliver between one and two batches with no duplicate event id — at most the active drain plus one deferred.

citations.anchor: it('keeps the pool usable when many units of work commit over a backlog'
citations.why: Twelve concurrent units of work over a 1200-row backlog, with subscribers that acquire their own client, all resolve and the pool ends with waitingCount 0 — the 'cannot be exhausted by drains' half.

citations.anchor: it('waits for a drain already in flight instead of abandoning it'
citations.why: onModuleDestroy is still pending while the gated drain runs and only resolves once the drain has finished.

citations.anchor: it('does not throw when the in-flight drain fails'
citations.why: A drain that rejects still leaves onModuleDestroy resolving undefined; the 'bounded by one batch' clause is not asserted anywhere.

citations.anchor: it('commits the events with the state change that produced them'
citations.why: Two events of kinds nobody subscribes to come back with attempts 0 after the post-commit drain, pinning the attempts clause; the 'marked delivered immediately' clause is not pinned — the test never reads dispatched_at.

citations.anchor: it('merges the actor into each payload without touching the inputs'
citations.why: Asserts the actor lands under the `actor` key of the returned payload while the input event, its payload and the array itself are untouched and not the same objects.

citations.anchor: it('overwrites an actor a producer had already put on the payload'
citations.why: A payload that already carried `actor` comes back with the application layer's actor instead — the overwrite clause.
